audit.whatIsWrong: All seven level rows contradicted the why text printed under them, in both layers.
audit.why: whys[0] and whys[1] describe Fiora bullying a Graves with no Quickdraw; whys[2], whys[3] and whys[5] each say the stage is even or contested; whys[4] gives level 6 to Fiora; whys[6] gives the late rows to Graves. The packet chart and the mirrored Fiora audit both read Fiora / Fiora / Skill / Skill / Fiora / Skill / Graves.
audit.corrected: Fiora (3/10), Fiora (3/10), Skill (5/10), Skill (5/10), Fiora (4/10), Skill (5/10), Graves (7/10).
sources: brief currentText content whys[0] through whys[6]

audit.whatIsWrong: Riposte is named the clock the lane runs on in eight places and never once given a cooldown; one line offers a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Riposte is 24/22/20/18/16s. At rank 1 that is a 24-second window in which she has no defensive answer — the single most useful number in this matchup, and the page rounds it to a wrong guess.
audit.corrected: Riposte is 24s at rank 1. Grand Challenge is 110s at rank 1 against your Collateral Damage at 100s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says in four places that Riposte stuns you when it parries your burst. It only stuns if it blocked an immobilizing effect — otherwise it slows. Graves has no immobilize in his kit at all.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'This stab slows the first enemy champion hit, or stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with this ability.' Graves' W is a brief slow, which is not an immobilize, and nothing else in his kit locks anyone down. So a solo Graves can never be stunned by Riposte — the punish for dumping burst into it is losing the damage, not being locked down.
audit.corrected: Riposte parries ALL your damage for its duration, which is why you never open with Collateral Damage — but on its own it can only slow you back. The stun needs an immobilize to block, and you do not have one; that only comes from your jungler's CC, so tell them to hold it.
sources: _kits/graves.json full ability list — no immobilizing effect

audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen is described as blinding her Vital-chasing autos in four places.
audit.why: Graves' W reduces sight range and briefly slows on impact — her attacks land normally inside it. What it actually does is make her lose sight of you mid-chase.
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen cuts her sight and slows on impact, so it breaks the chase rather than the attacks — do not stand in it expecting to be missed.

edits.before: Respect the first three levels — at level 1 you only have End of the Line and no Quickdraw to reposition, so Fiora just Lunges onto you, stamps a Vital, and procs it with an auto for percent-max-HP true damage that your True Grit armor can't reduce. Don't try to brawl back before your kit is up; last-hit with the tip of End of the Line and your spread shells, and accept the early Vital chip. Once you hit 3 with Quickdraw and Smoke Screen you can finally fight her on your terms: E in for the point-blank 4-shell burst, drop Smoke Screen so her Vital-procing autos and Bladework whiff in the blind, then E back out of her follow-up Lunge.
edits.after: Respect the first three levels — at level 1 you only have End of the Line and no Quickdraw to reposition, so Fiora just Lunges onto you, stamps a Vital, and procs it with an auto that your True Grit armor barely touches. Don't brawl back before your kit is up; last-hit with the tip of End of the Line and accept the early Vital chip. Once you hit 3 with Quickdraw and Smoke Screen you can fight her on your terms: dash in for the point-blank 4-shell burst, drop Smoke Screen so she loses sight of you rather than expecting her autos to miss, then leave before her follow-up Lunge lands.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a coin-flip skirmish — your True Grit armor stacks and two Quickdraw charges make extended trades playable, but Riposte is the clock the lane runs on. Bait the parry before you ever commit; if you dump R or a point-blank burst into Riposte she stuns you and proc-chains her Vitals to win it outright. At 6 her duel still edges yours, so treat Collateral Damage as a finisher or a wall-dash escape, not a poke — it's a slow shell she can sidestep. The real turn is your first item: Eclipse or Essence Reaver makes the Q-AA-E-AA point-blank pattern delete half her bar before crit Vitals catch up, and that's when you force every all-in.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a coin-flip skirmish — True Grit and a Quickdraw that refreshes off your autos make extended trades playable, but Riposte (24s at rank 1) is the clock the lane runs on. Bait the parry before you commit: everything you fire into it is simply erased, and she proc-chains Vitals from full afterwards. It only stuns if it blocks an immobilize, which you don't have — so that risk belongs to your jungler's CC, not to you. At 6 her duel still edges yours, so treat Collateral Damage as a finisher, never an opener. The turn is your first item, and that's when you force every all-in.

notes: BIGGEST FIND OF THIS SLICE: the page says four times that Riposte stuns you when it parries your burst. Riot's text is explicit that it stuns only if it blocked an IMMOBILIZING effect and otherwise just slows — and Graves has no immobilize anywhere in his kit (Smoke Screen is a brief slow). So a solo Graves cannot be stunned by Riposte at all; the real cost of dumping into it is losing a 100-second ultimate, and the stun risk transfers to whoever brings the jungler's CC. That changes how the whole all-in is played. Level chart: all seven rows contradicted their own why text and both the packet and the mirror agreed with the whys — flipped the lot as one atomic group, no why text needed changing for rows 1, 2, 6 or 7. 'Smoke Screen blind' fixed in four places. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: the page says Vitals deal 'percent-max-HP true damage' in four places. Riot's passive text gives neither a damage type nor a percent (only Grand Challenge carries a trueDamage flag), so I could not confirm it from the kits and did not rewrite those clauses.
